_comment: This organization's API rate limits, per model. Committed for the same
reason prices.json is: a campaign plan that depends on a limit must be
traceable to the limit it was planned against.
TPM and RPM can be read live from response headers (campaign_guard
ratelimits probes them, and a probe WINS over this file). TPD cannot —
OpenAI does not expose a daily counter in headers — so the daily cap is
only knowable from the dashboard, and only from this file at runtime.
TPD is the limit that matters at campaign scale: TPM bounds a burst,
TPD bounds the whole day. Hitting it stops every substrate at once until
Bump as_of whenever the dashboard changes (tier moves, model added).
source: OpenAI org dashboard, rate limits page, transcribed by the account owner
_notes: cursor-agent reaches the model through Cursor's backend, so its tokens
are limited and billed there and do NOT count against these numbers.
Whether CACHED input tokens count toward TPM/TPD is not stated in the
dashboard. The guards assume they DO (the conservative direction for
planning); pi and cursor sessions are ~95% cache, so the assumption
changes the campaign's daily footprint by roughly 2x. Confirm against
the usage page after the first paid day.
